analysis:
The PR changes CI routing in .github/workflows/provider-plan.yml and comments in provider-tests.yml. Head lines 183-185 drop the `required` flag from build-cluster, build-provider and cluster-release-checks. While job sizes are off, these lanes now ask the Darkbloom plane without a size, so they run on the approval's pinned macOS size instead of being forced onto Blacksmith. provider-tests.yml changes only comments (head lines 56-58 and 862-864). The `runs-on` expressions, steps, permissions, caches and secrets are unchanged.

No provider runtime, coordinator contract, attestation, key custody, encryption or prefix-cache code is touched. I found no regression against the canonical threats (T-041, TB-007, TB-011 and others).

The security-relevant effect is that the build jobs, which produce the test products and run release build checks, can now run on a Darkbloom Sandbox lane rather than Blacksmith. The workflow has `permissions: contents: read`, checks out with persist-credentials: false, and uses SAVE_CACHES only on push to master or dev. I saw no secrets exposed to those jobs in the supplied text.

Unverified contracts outside the evidence: darkbloom-route.yml, its approval pinning, and the trust and isolation of the Darkbloom plane runners. The build jobs feed the provider build and its caches, and cache poisoning from an untrusted runner is not evidenced here. These are infrastructure integration questions for later review, not findings. The release workflow is not in this batch.
